environment.description: Same Node.js Apollo GraphQL server deployed on EC2. Origin is fronted by a CloudFront distribution with a custom origin access configuration: the origin's security group restricts inbound to CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing) only. CloudFront distribution has a custom cache behavior for /graphql with Viewer Protocol Policy: HTTPS Only, and a CloudFront Function attached at viewer-request stage that validates a signed URL component (CloudFront Signature, Key-Pair-Id, Expires parameters) using a trusted key group. Requests missing valid signature receive 403. The signing key has 15-minute expiry and is issued only by the application's authenticated frontend BFF (backend-for-frontend) which itself requires a valid OAuth2 token before generating signed URLs. Additionally, CloudFront is configured with a custom header X-Origin-Verify with a rotating secret value that the origin ALB checks via a listener rule condition — requests without the matching header are dropped at the ALB level.

config.network: ALB security group inbound restricted to com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing prefix list
config.origin_verification: Custom header X-Origin-Verify checked by ALB listener rule, value rotated via Secrets Manager every 6 hours
config.signed_urls: CloudFront signed URLs required, trusted key group, 15-min expiry
config.signing_authority: BFF service issues signed URLs only after OAuth2 token validation
config.cache_behavior: CachingDisabled policy for /graphql, all query strings forwarded
